title: Space-Fillers and Lattice Moves: Which Solids Fill Space, Which Only Together, and Which Hold by Shape Alone
description:
Space-Fillers and Lattice Moves is Book Two (Earth) of The Five Orders of Space, by DICTO. It asks which solids fill space alone, which fill it only together, and which hold by shape alone, in ten chapters in three parts, a Closing, an Atlas of 28 plates and a methods appendix.

Part I, Alone. Chapter 1, The Dehn Test Picks Out the Lone Tilers of Two Sweeps (#100): on the sweep from the octahedron to the cube the Dehn invariant vanishes exactly at Kelvin's truncated octahedron and the cube; on the sweep from the cuboctahedron to the rhombic dodecahedron it vanishes for 1 ≤ μ ≤ 4/3 and at the B3 permutohedron, and the count of angles round an edge leaves only the rhombic dodecahedron. Chapter 2, Truncated Tetrahedra That Fill Space (#100): a tetrahedron with corner cuts is Dehn-zero exactly when the cuts add up to one edge, the octet's own ratio of two tetrahedra to every octahedron; all twelve integer cases with n ≤ 5, and one at n = 8, tile space, two pieces per period; conjecture for every rational cut; the seven golden cuts listed exactly. Chapter 3, One Move Each (#50): the classical space-fillers, each from one setting of Kaleidohedra's three lattice moves. Chapter 4, Blocks of Thirteen (#25, #26): a rhombic dodecahedron with its twelve face neighbours fills space by translation alone (8 of the 183 index-13 sublattices of fcc). Part II, Together. Chapter 5, The DICTO Jewel and the Stella Octangula (#41); Chapter 6, The Sunstar: Dodecahedra and Dogstars (#42); Chapter 7, One Level Up: Kagome Hulls and the DICTO Hexa (#17, #18); Chapter 8, Every Mix of the Platonic Solids Fills Space (#47, version 3), with a new section, The hybrid: one golden slab: the icosahedron of edge 1 in its skin stands in the dodecahedron's slab, so all five solids fill space in three slabs with five connectors; Chapter 9, The Admiral Cap Network: Only the Mixture Fills, and Never Face to Face (new): none of its three pieces fills space alone, at most 8 of 12 shared edges match round any corner, and the best arrangements are layers with one free flip per layer. Part III, Held. Chapter 10, Held by Shape Alone (#101): in a (111) layer of the octet every octahedron is locked and every tetrahedron free; in the Admiral layer of #47 every Admiral Cap and icosahedron is locked.

Closing, Back to the Brick: alone, very few; together, all of them; held, some; with what goes on in Book Three, DICTONIC Bonds, and Book Seven, The Permutohedron Paradigm. Atlas: 28 plates, one for each space-filling of the series that lives in another book or paper, with its DICTO DOI and home. Appendix: the Dehn screen, exact cover on the octet and the interlocking test, with their calibrations.

Scope: Goldberg's lists of six-, seven- and eight-faced space-fillers (Geometriae Dedicata, 1976–1981) were not available to us, so the members of the truncated-tetrahedron family of Chapter 2 with those face counts are new only as far as the sources checked show; any of them found in those lists will be credited to Goldberg in a later version.

91 pages. Cover by DICTO: a pillar of rock salt on the Fibonacci stacking, each ball piece carrying its layer letter, C or H, in reciprocal colours. Computation, verification and drafting with Claude (Anthropic). Licence CC BY-SA 4.0. More at dictospheres.com.
